user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a fully automated pipeline for building a Parallel Computing Service (PCS)-compatible Amazon Machine Image (AMI) using AWS Image Builder, designed to support multiple Linux distributions and both x86 and arm64 architectures for HPC workloads. The template must allow the user to select the target operating system from Amazon Linux 2, Rocky Linux 9, RHEL 9, or Ubuntu 22.04, and choose between x86 and arm64 architectures, with the ability to optionally specify a custom source AMI ID, Image Builder image ARN, or SSM parameter path; if no AMI is provided, the template should automatically resolve the appropriate base image using either hardcoded AMI IDs for Rocky Linux 9 (ami-067daee80a6d36ac0 for x86 and ami-034ee457b85b2fb4f for arm64) or SSM parameters for Amazon Linux 2 and Ubuntu 22.04, while RHEL 9 uses an Image Builder image ARN. The solution must create an IAM role and instance profile for EC2 with the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore and EC2InstanceProfileForImageBuilder managed policies, then deploy a nested stack from the aws-hpc-recipes S3 bucket (defaulting to the main branch) to provide Image Builder components for OS updates, reboot, performance optimization, CloudWatch agent, SSM agent, EFA installer, Lustre installer, EFS utilities installer, PCS agent installer, SLURM installer, Spack installer, and a reboot test. An Image Builder image recipe must be created that chains these components in the specified order, sets the parent image based on the user's selection or automatic lookup, configures a 64GB root volume on the appropriate device name for each distro (/dev/xvda for Amazon Linux 2, /dev/sda1 for others), and disables SSM agent uninstall after build. An infrastructure configuration must be created using the instance profile, requiring IMDSv2 with a hop limit of 1, and using default instance types like c6i.8xlarge and m6i.8xlarge for x86 or c7g.8xlarge and m7g.8xlarge for arm64. A distribution configuration must distribute the resulting AMI to the current region with a name pattern including the distro and architecture. An image pipeline must be created in an enabled state with image tests enabled and a 60-minute timeout, scheduled to run weekly on Sundays at 8:30 UTC using EXPRESSION_MATCH_ONLY execution condition, and with enhanced image metadata enabled. Additionally, a lifecycle policy must be created (except in GovCloud regions) using a dedicated IAM role with the EC2ImageBuilderLifecycleExecutionPolicy, configured to delete AMIs and their associated snapshots when they are older than 30 days while retaining at least 3 images, scoped to recipes matching the image recipe name and semantic version. Finally, the template must include a synchronous Image Builder image resource that depends on the pipeline to build the first version of the AMI during stack creation, and output the image pipeline reference and image name.

Parameters:
  SubnetId:
    Description: The subnet on which the app will run within the selected VPC.
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet::Id
  RunnerEgressGroupId:
    Description: The security group for the runner instance that allows outbound traffic.
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup::Id
  InstallId:
    Type: String
    Description: The install ID
  RunnerId:
    Type: String
    Description: The runner ID
  RunnerApiToken:
    Type: String
    Description: API token for the runner
  RunnerApiUrl:
    Type: String
    Description: API URL for the runner
    Default: https://runner.nuon.co
  RunnerInitScriptUrl:
    Type: String
    Description: URL for the init script that is added to the use data for the Runner ASG VM instances.
    Default: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nuonco/runner/refs/heads/main/scripts/aws/init.sh
  InstanceType:
    Type: String
    Description: EC2 instance type for the runner
    Default: t3a.medium
    AllowedValues:
    - t3.small
    - t3.medium
    - t3a.small
    - t3a.medium
    - t3a.large
    - m5.large
    - m5a.large
  RootVolumeSize:
    Type: Number
    Description: Size of the root EBS volume in GB
    Default: 30
    MinValue: 8
    MaxValue: 100

Resources:
  RunnerAutoScalingGroup:
    UpdatePolicy:

        MaxBatchSize: 1
        MinInstancesInService: 0
    Properties:
      LaunchTemplate:
        LaunchTemplateId:
          Ref: RunnerLaunchTemplate
        Version:
          Fn::GetAtt:
          - RunnerLaunchTemplate
          - LatestVersionNumber
      MaxSize: "1"
      MinSize: "1"
      Tags:
      - Key: nuon_runner_id
        PropagateAtLaunch: false
        Value:
          Ref: RunnerId
      - Key: Name

        Value:
          Fn::Sub: ${AWS::StackName}-runner

      - Ref: SubnetId
    Type: AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup

  RunnerInstanceProfile:
    Properties:

      - Ref: RunnerInstanceRole
    Type: AWS::IAM::InstanceProfile

  RunnerInstanceRole:

        - Action: sts:AssumeRole

      Policies:
      - PolicyDocument:
          Statement:
          - Action:
            - sts:AssumeIdentity

        PolicyName: RunnerInstancePolicy
      Tags:
      - Key: nuon_runner_id

          Ref: RunnerId
      - Key: runner.nuon.co/id
        Value:

      - Key: nuon_install_id

      - Key: Name
        Value:

    Type: AWS::IAM::Role

  # this is required to allow the runner ASG instances to access their metadata/tags

    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyName:
        Fn::Sub: ${RunnerId}-runner-instance-metadata

        Version: "2012-10-17"

        - Effect: Allow

  RunnerLaunchTemplate:

          DeviceIndex: 0
          Groups:
          - Ref: RunnerEgressGroupId
          SubnetId:
            Ref: SubnetId
        TagSpecifications:
        - ResourceType: instance
          Tags:
          - Key: nuon_runner_id
            Value:
              Ref: RunnerId
          - Key: runner.nuon.co/id
            Value:
              Ref: RunnerId
          - Key: nuon_runner_api_url
            Value:
              Ref: RunnerApiUrl
          - Key: nuon_runner_api_token
            Value:
              Ref: RunnerApiToken
          - Key: nuon_runner_id

The instance must not have a public IP, must be placed in a specified subnet (provided via the SubnetId parameter), and attached to a security group that allows outbound traffic (provided via the RunnerEgressGroupId parameter). AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: FSx for OpenZFS Single-AZ Filesystem.
  This template creates an FSx for OpenZFS filesystem with single-AZ deployment.
  It configures storage capacity, throughput, record size, and supports LZ4/ZSTD compression for optimized efficiency.
  Security groups enable required NFS ports (111, 2049, 20001-20003) with both TCP and UDP protocols for client access.
  The filesystem is deployed with NFS exports configured for cross-mount support and synchronous write operations.
  Use this template as a foundation for deploying NFS-based shared storage solutions.
  Refer to the Outputs tab for the filesystem ID, root volume ID, and security group ID needed to mount the filesystem.

### Stack metadata
Metadata:
  AWS::CloudFormation::Interface:
    ParameterGroups:
      - Label:
          default: Filesystem Options
        Parameters:
          - Capacity
          - Compression
          - ThroughputCapacity
          - RecordSize
      - Label:
          default: Networking and Access
        Parameters:
          - VpcId
          - SubnetId

Parameters:
  VpcId:
    Description: VPC where you will deploy the FSx filesystem
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC::Id
  SubnetId:
    Description: Subnet where you will deploy the FSx filesystem (must be in same VPC)
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet::Id
  Capacity:
    Description: Storage capacity (GiB)
    Type: Number
    Default: 256
  Compression:
    Description: Data compression type
    Type: String
    AllowedValues:
      - "LZ4"
      - "ZSTD"
      - "NONE"
    Default: "LZ4"
  RecordSize:
    Description: Record size in KiB for the root volume
    Type: Number
    Default: 128
    AllowedValues:
      - 4
      - 8
      - 16
      - 32
      - 64
      - 128
      - 256
      - 512
      - 1024
  ThroughputCapacity:
    Description: Throughput capacity for the filesystem (MBps)
    Type: Number
    Default: 64
    AllowedValues:
         - 64
         - 128
         - 256
         - 512
         - 1024
         - 2048
         - 3072
         - 4096

Resources:

  # Security group
  ZfsServerSG:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: 'Allows traffic to FSx for OpenZFS filesystem'
      GroupName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-fsxzfs-security-group'
      VpcId: !Ref VpcId

  # Clients join this group for access to an FSx for OpenZFS filesystem or volume
  ZfsClientSG:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: 'Clients join this group for access to FSx for OpenZFS filesystem or volume'
      GroupName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-fsxzfs-client-security-group'
      VpcId: !Ref VpcId

  ZfsServerSGInboundRule2049tcp:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::SecurityGroupIngress'
    Properties:
      IpProtocol: tcp
      Description: Allow incoming TCP connection from clients to NFS server daemon on port 2049
      FromPort: 2049
      ToPort: 2049
      GroupId: !Ref ZfsServerSG
      SourceSecurityGroupId: !Ref ZfsClientSG
  ZfsServerSGInboundRule2049udp:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::SecurityGroupIngress'
    Properties:
      IpProtocol: udp
      Description: Allow incoming UDP connection from clients to NFS server daemon on port 2049
      FromPort: 2049
      ToPort: 2049
      GroupId: !Ref ZfsServerSG
      SourceSecurityGroupId: !Ref ZfsClientSG
  ZfsServerSGInboundRule111tcp:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::SecurityGroupIngress'
    Properties:
      IpProtocol: tcp
      Description: Allow incoming TCP remote procedure call from client to NFS server on port 111
      FromPort: 111
      ToPort: 111
      GroupId: !Ref ZfsServerSG
      SourceSecurityGroupId: !Ref ZfsClientSG
  ZfsServerSGInboundRule111udp:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::SecurityGroupIngress'
    Properties:
      IpProtocol: udp
      Description: Allow incoming UDP remote procedure call from client to NFS server on port 111
      FromPort: 111
      ToPort: 111
      GroupId: !Ref ZfsServerSG
      SourceSecurityGroupId: !Ref ZfsClientSG
  ZfsServerSGInboundRule20001tcp:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::SecurityGroupIngress'
    Properties:
      IpProtocol: tcp
      Description: Allow incoming TCP traffic from client to NFS mount, status monitor, and lock daemons (ports 20001-20003)
      FromPort: 20001
      ToPort: 20003
      GroupId: !Ref ZfsServerSG
      SourceSecurityGroupId: !Ref ZfsClientSG
  ZfsServerSGInboundRule20001udp:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::SecurityGroupIngress'
    Properties:
      IpProtocol: udp
      Description: Allow incoming UDP traffic from client to NFS mount, status monitor, and lock daemons (ports 20001-20003
      FromPort: 20001
      ToPort: 20003
      GroupId: !Ref ZfsServerSG
      SourceSecurityGroupId: !Ref ZfsClientSG
  ZfsServerSGOutboundRuleClientSGAll:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::SecurityGroupEgress'
    Properties:
      Description: Allow egress to client from server
      IpProtocol: -1
      GroupId: !Ref ZfsServerSG
      DestinationSecurityGroupId: !Ref ZfsClientSG
  ZfsClientSGOutboundRuleServerSGAll:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::SecurityGroupEgress'
    Properties:
      Description: Allow egress to server from client
      IpProtocol: -1
      GroupId: !Ref ZfsClientSG
      DestinationSecurityGroupId: !Ref ZfsServerSG

  FSxOpenZFSFilesystem:
    Type: AWS::FSx::FileSystem
    DeletionPolicy: Delete
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Delete
    Properties:
      FileSystemType: OPENZFS
      StorageType: SSD
      StorageCapacity: !Ref Capacity
      SecurityGroupIds:
        - !Ref ZfsServerSG
      SubnetIds:
        - !Ref SubnetId
      OpenZFSConfiguration:
        DeploymentType: SINGLE_AZ_1
        ThroughputCapacity: !Ref ThroughputCapacity
        RootVolumeConfiguration:
          DataCompressionType: !Ref Compression
          RecordSizeKiB: !Ref RecordSize
          NfsExports:
            - ClientConfigurations:
                - Clients: "*"
                  Options: ["crossmnt", "sync", "rw"]

Outputs:
  FSxOpenZFSFilesystemId:
    Description: The ID of the FSxOpenZFS filesystem
    Value: !Ref FSxOpenZFSFilesystem
    Export:
      Name: !Sub ${AWS::StackName}-FSxOpenZFSFilesystemId
  FSxOpenZFSRootVolumeId:
    Description: The root volume ID for the FSxOpenZFS filesystem
    Value: !GetAtt FSxOpenZFSFilesystem.RootVolumeId
    Export:
      Name: !Sub ${AWS::StackName}-FSxOpenZFSRootVolumeId
  FSxOpenZFSSecurityGroupId:
    Description: Clients join this group for access to the FSx for OpenZFS filesystem or mount
    Value: !Ref ZfsClientSG
    Export:
      Name: !Sub ${AWS::StackName}-FSxOpenZFSSecurityGroupId
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a single-AZ FSx for OpenZFS filesystem for NFS-based shared storage, deployed in a specified VPC and subnet with 256 GiB of SSD storage by default, a throughput capacity of 64 MBps, a record size of 128 KiB for the root volume, and LZ4 data compression. The filesystem must be configured with NFS exports that allow all clients to mount it with crossmnt, sync, and rw options. Two security groups are required: a server security group for the FSx filesystem that allows NFS traffic from the client security group on ports 111 (TCP and UDP), 2049 (TCP and UDP), and 20001–20003 (TCP and UDP), and a client security group that clients use for access, with mutual egress rules between the server and client security groups to allow all traffic. The filesystem must be set to delete on stack deletion. The template should provide as outputs the filesystem ID, the root volume ID, and the client security group ID, all with export names scoped to the stack name.

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: 'Plot Palette - Step Functions Orchestration Stack'

Parameters:
  EnvironmentName:
    Type: String
    Default: production
    Description: Environment name for resource tagging
    AllowedValues:
      - development
      - staging
      - production

  JobsTableName:
    Type: String
    Description: DynamoDB Jobs table name

  JobsTableArn:
    Type: String
    Description: ARN of the Jobs DynamoDB table

  CheckpointMetadataTableName:
    Type: String
    Description: DynamoDB CheckpointMetadata table name

  CheckpointMetadataTableArn:
    Type: String
    Description: ARN of the CheckpointMetadata DynamoDB table

  EcsClusterArn:
    Type: String
    Description: ARN of the ECS cluster

  TaskDefinitionArn:
    Type: String
    Description: ARN of the ECS task definition

  SubnetIds:
    Type: CommaDelimitedList
    Description: Subnet IDs for ECS tasks

  SecurityGroupId:
    Type: String
    Description: Security Group ID for ECS tasks

  ECSTaskRoleArn:
    Type: String
    Description: ARN of the ECS task role

  ECSExecutionRoleArn:
    Type: String
    Description: ARN of the ECS execution role

  TemplatesBucketName:
    Type: String
    Description: S3 bucket containing the ASL definition file
    Default: ''

Conditions:
  UseDefaultBucket: !Equals [!Ref TemplatesBucketName, '']

Resources:
  StepFunctionsExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub 'plot-palette-SFNExecutionRole-${EnvironmentName}'
      Description: IAM role for Step Functions job lifecycle state machine
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: states.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ECSTaskManagement
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ecs:RunTask
                Resource:
                  - !Ref TaskDefinitionArn
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ecs:StopTask
                  - ecs:DescribeTasks
                Resource: '*'
                Condition:
                  ArnEquals:
                    ecs:cluster: !Ref EcsClusterArn
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: iam:PassRole
                Resource:
                  - !Ref ECSTaskRoleArn
                  - !Ref ECSExecutionRoleArn
        - PolicyName: DynamoDBAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - dynamodb:UpdateItem
                  - dynamodb:GetItem
                Resource:
                  - !Ref JobsTableArn
                  - !Ref CheckpointMetadataTableArn
        - PolicyName: EventBridgeAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - events:PutTargets
                  - events:PutRule
                  - events:DescribeRule
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:aws:events:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:rule/StepFunctionsGetEventsForECSTaskRule'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub 'plot-palette-sfn-role-${EnvironmentName}'
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName
        - Key: Project
          Value: plot-palette

  JobLifecycleStateMachine:
    Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
    Properties:
      StateMachineName: !Sub 'plot-palette-job-lifecycle-${EnvironmentName}'
      RoleArn: !GetAtt StepFunctionsExecutionRole.Arn
      DefinitionS3Location:
        Bucket: !If
          - UseDefaultBucket
          - !Sub 'plot-palette-cfn-${AWS::AccountId}-${AWS::Region}'
          - !Ref TemplatesBucketName
        Key: step-functions/job-lifecycle.asl.json
      DefinitionSubstitutions:
        JobsTableName: !Ref JobsTableName
        CheckpointMetadataTableName: !Ref CheckpointMetadataTableName
        EcsClusterArn: !Ref EcsClusterArn
        TaskDefinitionArn: !Ref TaskDefinitionArn
        SubnetIds: !Sub
          - '["${JoinedSubnets}"]'
          - JoinedSubnets: !Join ['","', !Ref SubnetIds]
        SecurityGroupId: !Ref SecurityGroupId
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub 'plot-palette-job-lifecycle-${EnvironmentName}'
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName
        - Key: Project
          Value: plot-palette

Outputs:
  StateMachineArn:
    Description: ARN of the Job Lifecycle state machine
    Value: !Ref JobLifecycleStateMachine
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-StateMachineArn'

  StateMachineName:
    Description: Name of the Job Lifecycle state machine
    Value: !GetAtt JobLifecycleStateMachine.Name
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-StateMachineName'

  StepFunctionsRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the Step Functions execution role
    Value: !GetAtt StepFunctionsExecutionRole.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-StepFunctionsRoleArn'
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Step Functions orchestration stack for the Plot Palette application, designed to manage job lifecycle workflows by coordinating ECS tasks and DynamoDB operations. The template must accept parameters for the environment name (with allowed values of development, staging, or production, defaulting to production), the DynamoDB Jobs table name and ARN, the DynamoDB CheckpointMetadata table name and ARN, the ECS cluster ARN, the ECS task definition ARN, a comma-delimited list of subnet IDs for ECS tasks, a security group ID for ECS tasks, the ECS task role ARN, the ECS execution role ARN, and an optional S3 bucket name for the ASL definition file (defaulting to an empty string). If the S3 bucket name is not provided, the template should use a default bucket named plot-palette-cfn-{accountId}-{region}. The core resource is an IAM role for Step Functions execution, named plot-palette-SFNExecutionRole-{environment}, which trusts the states.amazonaws.com service and includes policies for ECS task management (allowing ecs:RunTask on the specified task definition, ecs:StopTask and ecs:DescribeTasks on any resource with an ArnEquals condition on the ECS cluster, and iam:PassRole on both the ECS task role and execution role), DynamoDB access (allowing dynamodb:UpdateItem and dynamodb:GetItem on both the Jobs and CheckpointMetadata table ARNs), and EventBridge access (allowing events:PutTargets, events:PutRule, and events:DescribeRule on the rule ARN pattern arn:aws:events:{region}:{accountId}:rule/StepFunctionsGetEventsForECSTaskRule). The template must also create a Step Functions state machine named plot-palette-job-lifecycle-{environment}, referencing the IAM role, loading its definition from an S3 location with the key step-functions/job-lifecycle.asl.json, and using definition substitutions for the Jobs table name, CheckpointMetadata table name, ECS cluster ARN, task definition ARN, subnet IDs (formatted as a JSON array string), and security group ID. All resources must be tagged with Name, Environment, and Project keys set to plot-palette. The stack should export the state machine ARN, state machine name, and Step Functions role ARN as outputs with export names prefixed by the stack name.

          - Action:

            Effect: Allow
            Resource: !Sub "arn:${AWS::Partition}:s3:::${TargetBucketName}/*"
      Roles:
        - !Ref Role

  ReplicationRule:
    Type: Custom::ReplicationRule
    Version: "1.0"
    Properties:
      ServiceToken: !Sub "arn:${AWS::Partition}:lambda:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:function:custom-resource"
      AgentService: s3
      AgentType: client
      # https://boto3.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/reference/services/s3/client/put_bucket_replication.html
      AgentCreateMethod: put_bucket_replication
      AgentCreateArgs:
        Bucket: !Ref SourceBucketName

              Prefix: ""

                StorageClass: !Ref StorageClass
                EncryptionConfiguration:
                  ReplicaKmsKeyID: !Sub "arn:${AWS::Partition}:kms:${TargetBucketRegion}:${AWS::AccountId}:alias/aws/s3"
      AgentUpdateMethod: put_bucket_replication
      AgentUpdateArgs:
        Bucket: !Ref SourceBucketName
        ReplicationConfiguration:
          Role: !Sub "${Role.Arn}"
          Rules:
            - Status: Enabled
              SourceSelectionCriteria:
                SseKmsEncryptedObjects:
                  Status: Enabled
              Prefix: ""
              Destination:
                Bucket: !Sub "arn:${AWS::Partition}:s3:::${TargetBucketName}"
                StorageClass: !Ref StorageClass
                EncryptionConfiguration:
                  ReplicaKmsKeyID: !Sub "arn:${AWS::Partition}:kms:${TargetBucketRegion}:${AWS::AccountId}:alias/aws/s3"
      # https://boto3.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/reference/services/s3/client/delete_bucket_replication.html

Outputs:

The template must accept the following parameters: SourceBucketName, TargetBucketName, TargetBucketRegion, StorageClass (with a default of STANDARD), and CustomResourceVersion. It should create an IAM role that trusts the S3 service to assume the role, and attach a least-privilege policy granting s3:GetReplicationConfiguration, s3:ListBucket on the source bucket, s3:GetObjectVersion and s3:GetObjectVersionAcl on source objects, and s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateDelete on target objects. The custom resource must call the Lambda function using the service token arn:aws:lambda:<region>:<account>:function:custom-resource, and invoke the put_bucket_replication method for create and update operations, and delete_bucket_replication for deletion. The replication configuration must enable replication for all prefixes, include SSE-KMS encrypted objects, and specify a destination storage class set from the parameter, with encryption configuration using the default AWS managed KMS key alias aws/s3 in the target region. The template should output the logical ID of the IAM role and its ARN, each exported with the stack name as a prefix.

The template should create four interface VPC endpoints for the SSM, EC2Messages, SSMMessages, and EC2 services, each attached to the imported private subnet using the imported security group, with private DNS enabled. Resources:
  #------------------------------------------------------------
  # Create a VPC with a public and private subnet across two AZs
  #------------------------------------------------------------
  Pattern3VPC:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::VPC'
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: 172.31.0.0/16
      Tags:
      - Key: ResourceType
        Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  Pattern3PublicSubnet1:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::Subnet'
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Pattern3VPC
      AvailabilityZone: us-east-1a
      CidrBlock: 172.31.1.0/24
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: true
      Tags:
      - Key: Name
        Value: !Join ["-", [!Ref Pattern3VPC, "PublicSubnet1"]]
      - Key: ResourceType
        Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  Pattern3PublicSubnet2:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::Subnet'
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Pattern3VPC
      AvailabilityZone: us-east-1b
      CidrBlock: 172.31.3.0/24
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: true
      Tags:
      - Key: Name
        Value: !Join ["-", [!Ref Pattern3VPC, "PublicSubnet2"]]
      - Key: ResourceType
        Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  Pattern3PrivateSubnet1:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::Subnet'
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Pattern3VPC
      AvailabilityZone: us-east-1a
      CidrBlock: 172.31.2.0/24
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: false
      Tags:
      - Key: Name
        Value: !Join ["-", [!Ref Pattern3VPC, "PrivateSubnet1"]]
      - Key: ResourceType
        Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  Pattern3PrivateSubnet2:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::Subnet'
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Pattern3VPC
      AvailabilityZone: us-east-1b
      CidrBlock: 172.31.4.0/24
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: false
      Tags:
      - Key: Name
        Value: !Join ["-", [!Ref Pattern3VPC, "PrivateSubnet2"]]
      - Key: ResourceType
        Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  #-------------------------------------------------------------
  # Create an IGW and attach to the created VPC
  # Create a NAT GW with an associated public IP address.
  #-------------------------------------------------------------

  Pattern3IGW:
    Type: AWS::EC2::InternetGateway
    Properties:
      Tags:
      - Key: Name
        Value: !Join ["-", [!Ref Pattern3VPC, "igw"]]
      - Key: ResourceType
        Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  Pattern3IGWAttach:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Pattern3VPC
      InternetGatewayId: !Ref Pattern3IGW

  Pattern3NatGateway:
    Type: "AWS::EC2::NatGateway"
    DependsOn: Pattern3NatPublicIP
    Properties:
      AllocationId: !GetAtt Pattern3NatPublicIP.AllocationId
      SubnetId: !Ref Pattern3PublicSubnet1
      Tags:
      - Key: Name
        Value: !Join ["-", [!Ref Pattern3VPC, "nat"]]
      - Key: ResourceType
        Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  Pattern3NatPublicIP:
    Type: "AWS::EC2::EIP"
    DependsOn: Pattern3VPC
    Properties:
      Domain: vpc
      Tags:
      - Key: Name
        Value: !Join ["-", [!Ref Pattern3VPC, "NatPublicIP"]]
      - Key: ResourceType
        Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  #-------------------------------------------------------------
  # Create public route table and attach to the public subnets
  #-------------------------------------------------------------

  Pattern3PublicRouteTable1:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::RouteTable'
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Pattern3VPC
      Tags:
        - Key: Network
          Value: Public
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Join ["-", [!Ref Pattern3VPC, "PublicRouteTable1"]]
        - Key: ResourceType
          Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  Pattern3PublicRouteTable2:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::RouteTable'
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Pattern3VPC
      Tags:
        - Key: Network
          Value: Public
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Join ["-", [!Ref Pattern3VPC, "PublicRouteTable2"]]
        - Key: ResourceType
          Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  Pattern3PublicRoute1:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::Route'
    DependsOn:
      - Pattern3IGW
      - Pattern3IGWAttach
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref Pattern3PublicRouteTable1
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      GatewayId: !Ref Pattern3IGW

  Pattern3PublicRoute2:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::Route'
    DependsOn:
      - Pattern3IGW
      - Pattern3IGWAttach
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref Pattern3PublicRouteTable2
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      GatewayId: !Ref Pattern3IGW

  Pattern3PublicSubnet1RouteTableAssociation1:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation'
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref Pattern3PublicSubnet1
      RouteTableId: !Ref Pattern3PublicRouteTable1

  Pattern3PublicSubnet1RouteTableAssociation2:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation'
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref Pattern3PublicSubnet2
      RouteTableId: !Ref Pattern3PublicRouteTable2

  #-------------------------------------------------------------
  # Create public route table and attach to the public subnets
  #-------------------------------------------------------------

  Pattern3PrivateRouteTable1:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::RouteTable'
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Pattern3VPC
      Tags:
        - Key: Network
          Value: Public
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Join ["-", [!Ref Pattern3VPC, "PrivateRouteTable1"]]
        - Key: ResourceType
          Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  Pattern3PrivateRouteTable2:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::RouteTable'
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Pattern3VPC
      Tags:
        - Key: Network
          Value: Public
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Join ["-", [!Ref Pattern3VPC, "PrivateRouteTable2"]]
        - Key: ResourceType
          Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  Pattern3PrivateRoute1:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::Route'
    DependsOn: Pattern3IGW
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref Pattern3PrivateRouteTable1
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      NatGatewayId: !Ref Pattern3NatGateway

  Pattern3PrivateRoute2:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::Route'
    DependsOn: Pattern3IGW
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref Pattern3PrivateRouteTable2
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      NatGatewayId: !Ref Pattern3NatGateway

  Pattern3PrivateSubnet1RouteTableAssociation1:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation'
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref Pattern3PrivateSubnet1
      RouteTableId: !Ref Pattern3PrivateRouteTable1

  Pattern3PrivateSubnet1RouteTableAssociation2:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation'
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref Pattern3PrivateSubnet2
      RouteTableId: !Ref Pattern3PrivateRouteTable2
#---------------------------------------------------------
# Output section
#---------------------------------------------------------
Outputs:
  OutputPatternStackName:
    Description: Stack name
    Value: !Ref AWS::StackName
  OutputPattern3VPC:
    Description: Baseline VPC
    Value: !Ref Pattern3VPC
    Export:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-VpcId"
  OutputPattern3PublicSubnet1:
    Description: Public Subnet 1 VPC
    Value: !Ref Pattern3PublicSubnet1
    Export:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-PublicSubnet1"
  OutputPattern3PublicSubnet2:
    Description: Public Subnet 2 VPC
    Value: !Ref Pattern3PublicSubnet2
    Export:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-PublicSubnet2"
  OutputPattern3PrivateSubnet1:
    Description: Private Subnet 1 VPC
    Value: !Ref Pattern3PrivateSubnet1
    Export:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-PrivateSubnet1"
  OutputPattern3PrivateSubnet2:
    Description: Private Subnet 2 VPC
    Value: !Ref Pattern3PrivateSubnet2
    Export:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-PrivateSubnet2"
  OutputPatternStackName:
    Description: Stack name
    Value: !Ref AWS::StackName

The template should include an Internet Gateway attached to the VPC, a NAT Gateway in the first public subnet with an associated Elastic IP (domain vpc), and separate route tables for public and private subnets. Each subnet should be associated with its respective route table. The stack should export the VPC ID and all four subnet IDs with export names following the pattern "${AWS::StackName}-VpcId", "${AWS::StackName}-PublicSubnet1", "${AWS::StackName}-PublicSubnet2", "${AWS::StackName}-PrivateSubnet1", and "${AWS::StackName}-PrivateSubnet2", and also output the stack name itself.

    MaxLength: '255'
    Default: SomePlatform

  Component:
    Type: String
    MinLength: '3'
    MaxLength: '255'
    Default: App5-php

    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:

          Principal:
            Service: ec2.amazonaws.com
          Action: sts:AssumeRole

The template should accept parameters for an infrastructure name (defaulting to "main"), a project name, and an environment tag (either "nonprod" or "prod", defaulting to "nonprod"). The list of allowed CIDR blocks must be dynamically retrieved from an SSM parameter, with a default path of "/account/main/cidr-block/allowed/list". The WebACL should have a default action of block, and include a custom rule at priority 0 that allows traffic from the IP set created from that CIDR list, followed by four AWS managed rule groups at priorities 1 through 4: the Common Rule Set, the Amazon IP Reputation List, the Anonymous IP List, and the Known Bad Inputs Rule Set, all with no excluded rules and with their override action set to "None" (i.e., they take their default action). All rules must have CloudWatch metrics and sampled requests enabled, with appropriate metric names. The WebACL itself must have a visibility config with a metric name of "GlobalWebACLMetric". The resource should be tagged with the stack name, application, customer, contact-email, environment, and team, where the customer, contact-email, and team values are resolved from SSM parameters using the infrastructure name (e.g., "/account/main/tag/customer"). Additionally, the template must create an SSM parameter of type String with a name like "/waf/main/cloudfront/{projectName}/webacl" and value equal to the WebACL ARN, tagged identically. Finally, the stack should export the WebACL name, ARN, ID, and the SSM parameter name, type, and value as outputs for cross-stack references.

        Description: Do you want to load the default blueprints into sputnik ?
        Default: true
        AllowedValues:
            - true
            - false

Conditions:
    LoadDefaultsOnInstall: !Equals [ !Ref LoadDefaults, true ]

Mappings:
    Send:
        AnonymousUsage:
            Data: "Yes"
    SourceCode:
        App:
            ShortName: 'sputnik'
            FullName: 'sputnik - The Simple IoT Management System'
        General:
            S3Bucket: '%%BUCKET_NAME%%'
            KeyPrefix: 'sputnik/%%VERSION%%'

Resources:

    # ##########################################################################
    #
    # S3
    #
    # ##########################################################################
    # Nested stack - Data bucket creation
    CFStackForDataBucket:
        Type: AWS::CloudFormation::Stack
        Properties:
            TemplateURL: !Join ['/', ['https://s3.amazonaws.com', !Join ['-', ['%%BUCKET_NAME%%', Ref: 'AWS::Region']], !Join ['/', [!FindInMap ['SourceCode', 'General', 'KeyPrefix'], 'cf/sputnik-s3bucket-data.yml']]]]

    # Nested stack - Website bucket creation
    CFStackForWebsite:
        Type: AWS::CloudFormation::Stack
        Properties:
            TemplateURL: !Join ['/', ['https://s3.amazonaws.com', !Join ['-', ['%%BUCKET_NAME%%', Ref: 'AWS::Region']], !Join ['/', [!FindInMap ['SourceCode', 'General', 'KeyPrefix'], 'cf/sputnik-s3bucket-website.yml']]]]
            Parameters:
                IsWebsitePublic: !Ref IsWebsitePublic

    # ##########################################################################
    #
    # Cognito
    #
    # ##########################################################################
    # Nested stack - Cognito
    CFStackForCognito:
        Type: AWS::CloudFormation::Stack
        Properties:
            TemplateURL: !Join ['/', ['https://s3.amazonaws.com', !Join ['-', ['%%BUCKET_NAME%%', Ref: 'AWS::Region']], !Join ['/', [!FindInMap ['SourceCode', 'General', 'KeyPrefix'], 'cf/sputnik-cognito.yml']]]]
            Parameters:
                AdministratorName: !Ref AdministratorName
                AdministratorEmail: !Ref AdministratorEmail
                dataBucketArn: !GetAtt CFStackForDataBucket.Outputs.dataBucketArn
                websiteURL: !GetAtt CFStackForWebsite.Outputs.websiteUrl
                fullName: !FindInMap ['SourceCode', 'App', 'FullName']

    # ##########################################################################
    #
    # Dynamo DB
    #
    # ##########################################################################
    CFStackForDynamoDB:
        Type: AWS::CloudFormation::Stack
        Properties:
            TemplateURL: !Join ['/', ['https://s3.amazonaws.com', !Join ['-', ['%%BUCKET_NAME%%', Ref: 'AWS::Region']], !Join ['/', [!FindInMap ['SourceCode', 'General', 'KeyPrefix'], 'cf/sputnik-ddb-tables.yml']]]]

    # ##########################################################################
    #
    # Lambda
    #
    # ##########################################################################
    CFStackForLambdaHelpers:
        Type: AWS::CloudFormation::Stack
        Properties:
            TemplateURL: !Join ['/', ['https://s3.amazonaws.com', !Join ['-', ['%%BUCKET_NAME%%', Ref: 'AWS::Region']], !Join ['/', [!FindInMap ['SourceCode', 'General', 'KeyPrefix'], 'cf/sputnik-lambda-helpers.yml']]]]
            Parameters:
                sourceBucket: !Join ['-', [!FindInMap ['SourceCode', 'General', 'S3Bucket'], Ref: 'AWS::Region']]
                sourceKeyPrefix: !FindInMap ['SourceCode', 'General', 'KeyPrefix']
                destBucketArn: !GetAtt CFStackForWebsite.Outputs.websiteBucketArn
                dataBucketArn: !GetAtt CFStackForDataBucket.Outputs.dataBucketArn
                settingsTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.settingsTable
                devicesTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.devicesTable
                deviceTypesTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.deviceTypesTable
                deviceBlueprintsTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.deviceBlueprintsTable
                systemsTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.systemsTable
                systemBlueprintsTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.systemBlueprintsTable
                greengrassServiceRoleArn: !GetAtt greengrassServiceIAMRole.Arn

    CFStackForLambdaServices:
        Type: AWS::CloudFormation::Stack
        Properties:
            TemplateURL: !Join ['/', ['https://s3.amazonaws.com', !Join ['-', ['%%BUCKET_NAME%%', Ref: 'AWS::Region']], !Join ['/', [!FindInMap ['SourceCode', 'General', 'KeyPrefix'], 'cf/sputnik-lambda-services.yml']]]]
            Parameters:
                sourceBucket: !Join ['-', [!FindInMap ['SourceCode', 'General', 'S3Bucket'], Ref: 'AWS::Region']]
                sourceKeyPrefix: !FindInMap ['SourceCode', 'General', 'KeyPrefix']
                dataBucket: !GetAtt CFStackForDataBucket.Outputs.dataBucket
                settingsTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.settingsTable
                devicesTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.devicesTable
                deviceTypesTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.deviceTypesTable
                deviceBlueprintsTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.deviceBlueprintsTable
                deploymentsTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.deploymentsTable
                systemsTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.systemsTable
                systemBlueprintsTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.systemBlueprintsTable
                greengrassGroupsIAMRoleArn: !GetAtt greengrassGroupsIAMRole.Arn
                iotPolicyForGreengrassCores: !Ref IoTPolicyForGreengrassCores
                iotConnectPolicyForSputnikCertificates: !Ref IoTConnectPolicyForSputnikCertificates
                userPoolId: !GetAtt CFStackForCognito.Outputs.userPoolId
                iotEndpoint: !GetAtt iotEndpoint.endpointAddress
                appUUID: !GetAtt initAppUUID.UUID

    # ##########################################################################
    #
    # AppSync
    #
    # ##########################################################################
    CFStackForAppSync:
        Type: AWS::CloudFormation::Stack
        Properties:
            TemplateURL: !Join ['/', ['https://s3.amazonaws.com', !Join ['-', ['%%BUCKET_NAME%%', Ref: 'AWS::Region']], !Join ['/', [!FindInMap ['SourceCode', 'General', 'KeyPrefix'], 'cf/sputnik-appsync.yml']]]]
            Parameters:
                sourceBucket: !Join ['-', [!FindInMap ['SourceCode', 'General', 'S3Bucket'], Ref: 'AWS::Region']]
                sourceKeyPrefix: !Join ['/', [!FindInMap ['SourceCode', 'General', 'KeyPrefix'], 'cf' ]]
                userPoolId: !GetAtt CFStackForCognito.Outputs.userPoolId
                settingsTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.settingsTable
                dataStoreTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.dataStoreTable
                devicesTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.devicesTable
                deviceTypesTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.deviceTypesTable
                deviceBlueprintsTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.deviceBlueprintsTable
                deploymentsTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.deploymentsTable
                systemsTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.systemsTable
                systemBlueprintsTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.systemBlueprintsTable
                adminServiceLambdaFunctionArn: !GetAtt CFStackForLambdaServices.Outputs.adminServiceLambdaFunctionArn
                devicesServiceLambdaFunctionArn: !GetAtt CFStackForLambdaServices.Outputs.devicesServiceLambdaFunctionArn
                settingsServiceLambdaFunctionArn: !GetAtt CFStackForLambdaServices.Outputs.settingsServiceLambdaFunctionArn
                deploymentsServiceLambdaFunctionArn: !GetAtt CFStackForLambdaServices.Outputs.deploymentsServiceLambdaFunctionArn
                systemsServiceLambdaFunctionArn: !GetAtt CFStackForLambdaServices.Outputs.systemsServiceLambdaFunctionArn
                utilsCustomResourceLambdaFunctionArn: !GetAtt CFStackForLambdaHelpers.Outputs.utilsCustomResourceLambdaFunctionArn

    # ##########################################################################
    #
    # CloudTrail
    #
    # ##########################################################################
    CFStackForCloudTrail:
        Type: AWS::CloudFormation::Stack
        Properties:
            TemplateURL: !Join ['/', ['https://s3.amazonaws.com', !Join ['-', ['%%BUCKET_NAME%%', Ref: 'AWS::Region']], !Join ['/', [!FindInMap ['SourceCode', 'General', 'KeyPrefix'], 'cf/sputnik-cloudtrail.yml']]]]

    # Greengrass Service Role
    greengrassServiceIAMRole:
        Type: 'AWS::IAM::Role'
        Properties:
            AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
                Version: '2012-10-17'
                Statement:
                    - Effect: 'Allow'
                      Principal:
                          Service:
                              - 'greengrass.amazonaws.com'
                      Action:
                          - 'sts:AssumeRole'
            Path: '/'
            ManagedPolicyArns:
                - 'arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSGreengrassResourceAccessRolePolicy'

    # Systems Greengrass group role
    # NOTE: This is placed here, because else it creates a circular dependency between the Lambda Stack and the Systems Stack.
    greengrassGroupsIAMRole:
        Type: 'AWS::IAM::Role'
        Properties:
            AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
                Version: '2012-10-17'
                Statement:
                    - Effect: 'Allow'
                      Principal:
                          Service:
                              - 'greengrass.amazonaws.com'
                      Action:
                          - 'sts:AssumeRole'
            Path: '/'

    # Systems IoT Policy for Greengrass devices
    # NOTE: This is placed here, because else it creates a circular dependency between the Lambda Stack and the Systems Stack.
    IoTPolicyForGreengrassCores:
        Type: "AWS::IoT::Policy"
        DeletionPolicy: Retain
        Properties:
            PolicyDocument:
                Version: "2012-10-17"
                Statement:
                    -
                        Effect: "Allow"
                        Action:
                            - "iot:*"
                            - "greengrass:*"
                        Resource:
                            - "*"

    IoTConnectPolicyForSputnikCertificates:
        Type: "AWS::IoT::Policy"
        Properties:
            PolicyDocument:
                Version: "2012-10-17"
                Statement:
                    -
                        Effect: "Allow"
                        Action: "iot:Connect"
                        Resource:
                            - !Join [':', ['arn:aws:iot', Ref: 'AWS::Region', Ref: 'AWS::AccountId', 'client/${iot:Certificate.Subject.CommonName}']]
                            - !Join [':', ['arn:aws:iot', Ref: 'AWS::Region', Ref: 'AWS::AccountId', 'client/${iot:Certificate.Subject.CommonName}-*']]
                        Condition:
                            StringEquals:
                                iot:Certificate.Subject.Organization: "sputnik"
                    -
                        Effect: "Allow"
                        Action: "greengrass:Discover"
                        Resource:
                            - "*"

    # ##########################################################################
    #
    # Init
    #
    # ##########################################################################

    iotEndpoint:
        Type: 'Custom::Lambda'
        Properties:
            ServiceToken: !GetAtt CFStackForLambdaHelpers.Outputs.utilsCustomResourceLambdaFunctionArn
            Region: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
            customAction: 'iotDescribeEndpoint'
            # endpointType: 'iot:Data'
            endpointType: 'iot:Data-ATS'

    greengrassAssociateServiceRoleToAccount:
        Type: 'Custom::Lambda'
        Properties:
            ServiceToken: !GetAtt CFStackForLambdaHelpers.Outputs.utilsCustomResourceLambdaFunctionArn
            Region: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
            customAction: 'greengrassAssociateServiceRoleToAccount'

    # Initialization - Copy of website assets (html/js/css/assets)
    website:
        Type: 'Custom::LoadLambda'
        Properties:
            ServiceToken: !GetAtt CFStackForLambdaHelpers.Outputs.customResourceS3HelperArn
            Region: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
            sourceS3Bucket: !Join ['-', [!FindInMap ['SourceCode', 'General', 'S3Bucket'], Ref: 'AWS::Region']]
            sourceS3Key: !Join ['/', [!FindInMap ['SourceCode', 'General', 'KeyPrefix'], 'console']]
            destS3Bucket: !GetAtt CFStackForWebsite.Outputs.websiteBucket
            customAction: 'copyS3assets'

    websiteConfig:
        Type: 'Custom::LoadLambda'
        Properties:
            ServiceToken: !GetAtt CFStackForLambdaHelpers.Outputs.customResourceS3HelperArn
            Region: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
            destS3Bucket: !GetAtt CFStackForWebsite.Outputs.websiteBucket
            destS3Key: 'assets/appVariables.js'
            varName: 'appVariables'
            file:
                VERSION: '%%VERSION%%'
                USER_POOL_ID: !GetAtt CFStackForCognito.Outputs.userPoolId
                USER_POOL_CLIENT_ID: !GetAtt CFStackForCognito.Outputs.websiteCognitoClientId
                IDENTITY_POOL_ID: !GetAtt CFStackForCognito.Outputs.identityPool
                REGION: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
                IOT_COGNITO_POLICY: !GetAtt CFStackForCognito.Outputs.websiteCognitoIoTPolicy
                S3_DATA_BUCKET: !GetAtt CFStackForDataBucket.Outputs.dataBucket
                APP_SYNC_GRAPHQL_ENDPOINT: !GetAtt CFStackForAppSync.Outputs.appSyncGraphQLUrl
                IOT_ENDPOINT: !GetAtt iotEndpoint.endpointAddress
            customAction: 'putFile'

    # Initialization - Init Settings
    initSettings:
        Type: 'Custom::LoadLambda'
        Properties:
            ServiceToken: !GetAtt CFStackForLambdaHelpers.Outputs.utilsCustomResourceLambdaFunctionArn
            Region: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
            ddbTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.settingsTable
            ddbItem:
                id: "app-config"
                type: "config"
                setting:
                    uuid: !GetAtt initAppUUID.UUID
                    mapboxToken: "NA"
                    anonymousData: !FindInMap ["Send", "AnonymousUsage", "Data"]
            customAction: 'dynamodbSaveItem'

    # Initialization - UUID
    initAppUUID:
        Type: "Custom::LoadLambda"
        Properties:
            ServiceToken: !GetAtt CFStackForLambdaHelpers.Outputs.utilsCustomResourceLambdaFunctionArn
            Region: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
            customAction: "createUUID"
            anonymousData: !FindInMap ["Send", "AnonymousUsage", "Data"]
            version: '%%VERSION%%'

    # ##########################################################################
    #
    # Defaults
    #
    # ##########################################################################
    CFStackForDefaults:
        Type: AWS::CloudFormation::Stack
        Condition: LoadDefaultsOnInstall
        Properties:
            TemplateURL: !Join ['/', ['https://s3.amazonaws.com', !Join ['-', ['%%BUCKET_NAME%%', Ref: 'AWS::Region']], !Join ['/', [!FindInMap ['SourceCode', 'General', 'KeyPrefix'], 'cf/defaults/sputnik-defaults.yml']]]]
            Parameters:
                sourceS3Bucket: !Join ['-', [!FindInMap ['SourceCode', 'General', 'S3Bucket'], Ref: 'AWS::Region']]
                sourceS3KeyPrefix: !FindInMap ['SourceCode', 'General', 'KeyPrefix']
                deviceTypesTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.deviceTypesTable
                deviceBlueprintsTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.deviceBlueprintsTable
                systemBlueprintsTable: !GetAtt CFStackForDynamoDB.Outputs.systemBlueprintsTable
                utilsCustomResourceLambdaFunctionArn: !GetAtt CFStackForLambdaHelpers.Outputs.utilsCustomResourceLambdaFunctionArn
                greengrassGroupsIAMRole: !Ref greengrassGroupsIAMRole
                dataS3Bucket: !GetAtt CFStackForDataBucket.Outputs.dataBucket
                dataS3BucketArn: !GetAtt CFStackForDataBucket.Outputs.dataBucketArn

Outputs:
    # UUID
    AppUUID:
        Description: "App UUID"
        Value: !GetAtt initAppUUID.UUID
    # Website
    websiteUrl:
        Description: 'sputnik Website URL'
        Value: !GetAtt CFStackForWebsite.Outputs.websiteUrl
    # Cognito
    userPoolArn:
        Description: "sputnik User Pool"
        Value: !GetAtt CFStackForCognito.Outputs.userPoolArn
    userPoolId:
        Description: "sputnik User Pool ID"
        Value: !GetAtt CFStackForCognito.Outputs.userPoolId
    websiteCognitoClientId:
        Description: "sputnik Website Cognito Client"
        Value: !GetAtt CFStackForCognito.Outputs.websiteCognitoClientId
    identityPool:
        Description: "sputnik Identity Pool"
        Value: !GetAtt CFStackForCognito.Outputs.identityPool
    websiteCognitoIoTPolicy:
        Description: "IoT Policy to access resources"
        Value: !GetAtt CFStackForCognito.Outputs.websiteCognitoIoTPolicy
    # IOT
    iotEndpoint:
        Description: "IoT Endpoint"
        Value: !GetAtt iotEndpoint.endpointAddress
    greengrassGroupsIAMRole:
        Description: "IAM Role For Greengrass Groups to be used by Addons"
        Value: !Ref greengrassGroupsIAMRole
    # dataBucketAccessPolicy:
    #     Description: "IAM Policy to access the sputnik Data bucket"
    #     Value: !GetAtt CFStackForDataBucket.Outputs.dataBucketAccessPolicy
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates an IoT Pilot Kickstart solution called "sputnik" (Simple IoT Management System) to define, manage, and monitor IoT devices, incorporating a set of nested stacks for S3, Cognito, DynamoDB, Lambda, AppSync, CloudTrail, and IAM resources, with parameters for the administrator's name (AdministratorName) and email (AdministratorEmail, validated against a standard email pattern), a boolean IsWebsitePublic to decide whether the public S3 website is accessible, and a boolean LoadDefaults to optionally load default blueprints upon installation. The template should use mappings for anonymous usage data (Send mapping with "Yes") and source code references (SourceCode mapping with App short name 'sputnik' and full name 'sputnik - The Simple IoT Management System', and General key S3Bucket and KeyPrefix placeholders like %%BUCKET_NAME%% and %%VERSION%%). It must create a data bucket and a website bucket via nested stacks, conditionally make the website public, and set up a Cognito user pool with identity pool, user pool client, and an IoT policy for the website, referencing the data bucket ARN and website URL. DynamoDB tables for settings, devices, device types, device blueprints, systems, system blueprints, deployments, and data store should be created via another nested stack. Lambda helper and service functions (from separate nested stacks) must be deployed, receiving links to the source bucket, key prefix, S3 bucket ARNs, all DynamoDB table names, user pool ID, IoT endpoint, app UUID, and IAM roles for Greengrass. An AppSync GraphQL API stack should be provisioned, connected to the same DynamoDB tables and Lambda function ARNs, with Cognito user pool authentication. A CloudTrail stack is also needed. Two IAM roles must be defined: one for the Greengrass service role with the AWSGreengrassResourceAccessRolePolicy managed policy, and another for Greengrass groups (with no attached policies initially). Two IoT policies are required: IoTPolicyForGreeng

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Link AWS account with ReadOnly to Spot by NetApp
Parameters:
  Token:
    Description: The API Token for Spot.io
    Type: String
    AllowedPattern: ^[a-zA-Z0-9]+$
    NoEcho: true
Resources:
  SpotManagedPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy
    Properties:
      Description: Spot.io Account Policy
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: ReadonlyAccess
            Action:
              - autoscaling:Describe*
              - ec2:Describe*
              - elasticmapreduce:Describe*
              - elasticmapreduce:List*
              - elasticloadbalancing:Describe*
              - elasticbeanstalk:Describe*
              - iam:ListAccountAliases
            Effect: Allow
            Resource:
              - '*'
          - Sid: AccessEks
            Action:
              - eks:ListClusters
            Effect: Allow
            Resource:
              - '*'
          - Sid: AccessECS
            Action:
              - ecs:List*
              - ecs:Describe*
            Effect: Allow
            Resource:
              - '*'
          - Sid: AccessBatch
            Action:
              - batch:List*
              - batch:Describe*
            Effect: Allow
            Resource:
              - '*'
          - Sid: AccessCodeDeploy
            Action:
              - codedeploy:BatchGetDeployments
              - codedeploy:List*
            Effect: Allow
            Resource:
              - '*'
          - Sid: SavingsPlan
            Action:
              - savingsplans:Describe*
              - savingsplans:List*
            Effect: Allow
            Resource:
              - '*'
          - Sid: Lambda
            Action:
              - lambda:ListFunctions
            Effect: Allow
            Resource:
              - '*'
  SpotAccount:
    Type: Custom::SpotAccount
    Properties:
      ServiceToken: !Sub
        - arn:aws:lambda:${Region}:178579023202:function:onboarding-stackset-account-lambda
        - Region: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
      AwsAccountId: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      Token: !Ref 'Token'
    DependsOn:
      - 'SpotManagedPolicy'
  SpotExternalId:
    Type: Custom::SpotExternalId
    Properties:
      ServiceToken: !Sub
        - arn:aws:lambda:${Region}:178579023202:function:onboarding-stackset-external-id-lambda
        - Region: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
      SpotAccountId: !Ref 'SpotAccount'
      Token: !Ref 'Token'
    DependsOn:
     - "SpotAccount"
  SpotRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: arn:aws:iam::922761411349:root
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                sts:ExternalId: !Ref 'SpotExternalId'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Ref 'SpotManagedPolicy'
    DependsOn:
      - "SpotAccount"
      - "SpotExternalId"
  SpotLinkedCredentials:
    Type: Custom::SpotLinkedCredentials
    Properties:
      ServiceToken: !Sub
        - arn:aws:lambda:${Region}:178579023202:function:spotinst-set-credentials
        - Region: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
      AccountId: !Ref 'SpotAccount'
      IamRoleArn: !GetAtt 'SpotRole.Arn'
      Token: !Ref 'Token'
      StackId: !Ref 'AWS::StackId'
      isTokenEncrypted: "false"
    DependsOn:
      - 'SpotAccount'
      - 'SpotExternalId'
      - 'SpotRole'
  RenamedSpotAccountByAlias:
    Type: Custom::RenamedSpotAccountByAlias
    Properties:
      ServiceToken: !Sub
        - arn:aws:lambda:${Region}:178579023202:function:onboarding-stackset-alias-lambda
        - Region: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
      SpotAccountId: !Ref 'SpotAccount'
      Token: !Ref 'Token'
      AwsAccountId: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
    DependsOn:
      - 'SpotAccount'
      - 'SpotLinkedCredentials'
Outputs:
  AccountId:
    Description: The Account ID for Spot.io
    Value: !Ref 'SpotAccount'
  ExternalId:
    Description: The External ID for Spot.io Role
    Value: !Ref 'SpotExternalId'
  SpotRoleArn:
    Description: The Account Role ARN used for Spot.io
    Value: !GetAtt 'SpotRole.Arn'
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates the necessary IAM infrastructure and custom resources to link an AWS account with read-only access to Spot by NetApp, using an API token provided as a parameter that must be alphanumeric and hidden from output. The template should create a managed IAM policy that grants read-only access across a comprehensive set of AWS services including autoscaling, EC2, EMR, Elastic Load Balancing, Elastic Beanstalk, IAM account aliases, EKS cluster listing, ECS describe and list operations, Batch, CodeDeploy, Savings Plans, and Lambda function listing. It should then create a custom resource that registers the AWS account with Spot by invoking the Lambda function at the ARN arn:aws:lambda:${region}:178579023202:function:onboarding-stackset-account-lambda, passing the AWS account ID and the token. Following that, another custom resource should generate an external ID by invoking the Lambda function at arn:aws:lambda:${region}:178579023202:function:onboarding-stackset-external-id-lambda, using the Spot account ID from the first custom resource and the token. An IAM role should be created that trusts the Spot root account arn:aws:iam::922761411349:root with a condition requiring the external ID generated by the previous custom resource, and it should attach the managed policy created earlier. A custom resource should then link the credentials by invoking the Lambda function at arn:aws:lambda:${region}:178579023202:function:spotinst-set-credentials, passing the Spot account ID, the IAM role ARN, the token, the CloudFormation stack ID, and indicating the token is not encrypted. Finally, a custom resource should rename the Spot account by alias by invoking the Lambda function at arn:aws:lambda:${region}:178579023202:function:onboarding-stackset-alias-lambda, passing the Spot account ID, the token, and the AWS account ID. The template must ensure proper dependency ordering so that the account registration happens before external ID generation, the role is created after both the account and external ID exist, the credentials are linked after the role is created, and the alias renaming happens after the account is registered and credentials are linked. The template should output the Spot account ID, the external ID, and the IAM role ARN for reference.

Description: 'A CloudFormation template which shows how to provide multiple values to one StringValue when creating a DataPipeline definition, This template is entirely based on the example provided in the DataPipeline documentation here: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/datapipeline/latest/DeveloperGuide/dp-object-emrconfiguration.html - Written by Nishant Casey'

Resources:
  DynamoDBInputS3OutputHive:
    Type: AWS::DataPipeline::Pipeline
    Properties:
      Name: DynamoDBInputS3OutputHive
      Description: Pipeline to backup DynamoDB data to S3
      Activate: "true"
      PipelineObjects:
        - Id: ResourceId_I1mCc
          Name: ReleaseLabelCluster
          Fields:
            - Key: releaseLabel
              StringValue: emr-4.1.0
            - Key: applications
              StringValue: spark
            - Key: applications
              StringValue: hive
            - Key: applications
              StringValue: pig
            - Key: type
              StringValue: EmrCluster
            - Key: configuration
              RefValue: coresite
        - Id: coresite
          Name: coresite
          Fields:
            - Key: type
              StringValue: EmrConfiguration
            - Key: classification
              StringValue: core-site
            - Key: property
              RefValue: io-file-buffer-size
            - Key: property
              RefValue: fs-s3-block-size
        - Id: io-file-buffer-size
          Name: io-file-buffer-size
          Fields:
            - Key: type
              StringValue: Property
            - Key: value
              StringValue: "4096"
            - Key: key
              StringValue: io.file.buffer.size
        - Id: fs-s3-block-size
          Name: fs-s3-block-size
          Fields:
            - Key: type
              StringValue: Property
            - Key: value
              StringValue: "67108864"
            - Key: key
              StringValue: fs.s3.block.size
        - Id: DefaultSchedule
          Name: RunOnce
          Fields:
            - Key: occurrences
              StringValue: "1"
            - Key: startAt
              StringValue: FIRST_ACTIVATION_DATE_TIME
            - Key: type
              StringValue: Schedule
            - Key: period
              StringValue: 1 Day
        - Id: Default
          Name: Default
          Fields:
            - Key: resourceRole
              StringValue: DataPipelineDefaultResourceRole

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: 2010-09-09
Description: aws-cloudformation-templates/security/securitylake sets Amazon Security Lake.

Metadata:

Parameters:

    Type: String

  Environment:
    Type: String
    Default: production
    AllowedValues:
      - production
      - test
      - development
  TagKey:
    Type: String
    Default: createdby
    AllowedPattern: .+
  TagValue:
    Type: String
    Default: aws-cloudformation-templates
    AllowedPattern: .+

Conditions:
  CreateSubscriberForSIEM: !Not [ !Equals [!Ref AuditAccountId , ''] ]

  # IAM Role
  IAMRoleForSecurityLake:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: 2012-10-17
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Description: A role required for Security Lake to access logs.
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonSecurityLakeMetastoreManager
      Path: /service-role/

      Tags:
        - Key: environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: !Ref TagKey
          Value: !Ref TagValue
  # Security Lake
  CloudTrailLog:
    DependsOn:
      - DataLake
    Type: AWS::SecurityLake::AwsLogSource
    Properties:
      DataLakeArn: !GetAtt DataLake.Arn
      SourceName: CLOUD_TRAIL_MGMT
      SourceVersion: 2.0
  LambdaExecutionLog:
    DependsOn:
      - DataLake
      - CloudTrailLog
    Type: AWS::SecurityLake::AwsLogSource
    Properties:
      DataLakeArn: !GetAtt DataLake.Arn
      SourceName: LAMBDA_EXECUTION
      SourceVersion: 2.0
  EKSAuditLog:
    DependsOn:
      - DataLake
      - CloudTrailLog
      - LambdaExecutionLog
    Type: AWS::SecurityLake::AwsLogSource
    Properties:
      DataLakeArn: !GetAtt DataLake.Arn
      SourceName: EKS_AUDIT
      SourceVersion: 2.0
  Route53Log:
    DependsOn:
      - DataLake
      - CloudTrailLog
      - LambdaExecutionLog
      - EKSAuditLog
    Type: AWS::SecurityLake::AwsLogSource
    Properties:
      DataLakeArn: !GetAtt DataLake.Arn
      SourceName: ROUTE53
      SourceVersion: 2.0
  SecurityHubLog:
    DependsOn:
      - DataLake

      - LambdaExecutionLog

    Type: AWS::SecurityLake::AwsLogSource
    Properties:

    DependsOn:

      - CloudTrailLog
      - LambdaExecutionLog
      - EKSAuditLog
      - Route53Log
      - SecurityHubLog
    Type: AWS::SecurityLake::AwsLogSource
    Properties:
      DataLakeArn: !GetAtt DataLake.Arn
      SourceName: VPC_FLOW
      SourceVersion: 2.0

    Type: AWS::SecurityLake::DataLake

      MetaStoreManagerRoleArn: !GetAtt IAMRoleForSecurityLake.Arn

        - Key: environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: !Ref TagKey
          Value: !Ref TagValue
  SubscriberForSIEM:
    DependsOn:
      - CloudTrailLog
      - LambdaExecutionLog
      - EKSAuditLog
      - Route53Log
      - SecurityHubLog
      - VPCFlowLog

    Type: AWS::SecurityLake::Subscriber
    Properties:
      AccessTypes:
        - S3
      DataLakeArn: !GetAtt DataLake.Arn

        - AwsLogSource:
            SourceName: LAMBDA_EXECUTION
            SourceVersion: 2.0
        - AwsLogSource:
            SourceName: EKS_AUDIT
            SourceVersion: 2.0
        - AwsLogSource:

        - AwsLogSource:

            SourceVersion: 2.0
        - AwsLogSource:
            SourceName: VPC_FLOW
            SourceVersion: 2.0

      SubscriberName: Audit
      Tags:
        - Key: environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: !Ref TagKey
          Value: !Ref TagValue

    Condition: CreateSubscriberForSIEM

The template must accept an AuditAccountId parameter, which defaults to an empty string, and if a valid account ID is provided, it should conditionally create an S3-based subscriber named Audit that grants that account access to all log sources using the principal ID from the parameter and an external ID of SIEM. The deployment must include an IAM role named using the LogicalName parameter (defaulting to SecurityLake) followed by -SecurityLake and the region, with a path of /service-role/, and it must be attached to the AWS managed policy AmazonSecurityLakeMetastoreManager, with a trust policy allowing the Lambda service to assume the role. All resources must be tagged with an environment tag whose value comes from the Environment parameter (allowed values: production, test, development, defaulting to production), and a custom tag pair where the key defaults to createdby and the value defaults to aws-cloudformation-templates. The template should also expose a LogicalName parameter defaulting to SecurityLake to serve as a custom prefix for the IAM role name.

    AllowedPattern: ^(([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])\.){3}([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])(\/([1-2][0-8]))$

      SecurityGroupIngress:

  SSHSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup

          IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          Description: "SSH access"
      VpcId: !Ref VpcId
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub "${AWS::StackName} - SSH Access"

    Description: "SSH Security Group Id"
    Value: !Ref SSHSecurityGroup

  BastionHostSGId:
    Description: "Bastion Host Security Group Id"
    Value: !Ref BastionHostSecurityGroup

The template should accept an existing VPC ID as a parameter, along with a user-provided public IP address in CIDR notation (formatted as x.x.x.x/32) that will be used to allow SSH access from the user's current location, and it should also accept CIDR ranges for both a default public subnet (defaulting to 172.31.32.0/20) and the new private subnet (defaulting to 172.31.48.0/20), with validation ensuring these CIDR blocks fall within /16 to /28 ranges. The private subnet must be created with the MapPublicIpOnLaunch property set to false to ensure it remains private, and it should be tagged with the stack name for identification. A dedicated route table should be created for this private subnet and explicitly associated with it, also tagged with the stack name. For security groups, create one that allows SSH (TCP port 22) inbound traffic only from the specified default public subnet CIDR range, intended to permit access from a bastion host, and another that allows SSH inbound traffic only from the user's provided public IP address, with both security groups properly tagged and associated with the specified VPC. The template should output the IDs of both security groups, the private subnet ID, and the private route table ID so they can be referenced by other stacks or resources.

Description: Mozilla federated Admin ReadOnly ViewOnly IAM roles
Metadata:
  Source: https://github.com/mozilla/security/tree/master/operations/cloudformation-templates/infosec-dev_oidc_federated_roles.yaml
Resources:
  AdminIAMRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: MAWS-Admin
      Description: !Join [ '', [ 'AdministratorAccess Federated IAM Role which the group team_opsec is permitted to assume']]
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Principal:
              Federated: !Join [ '', [ 'arn:aws:iam::', !Ref 'AWS::AccountId', ':oidc-provider/auth.mozilla.auth0.com/' ]]
            Action: sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
            Effect: Allow
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                auth.mozilla.auth0.com/:aud: N7lULzWtfVUDGymwDs0yDEq6ZcwmFazj
              ForAnyValue:StringEquals:
                auth.mozilla.auth0.com/:amr:
                  - team_opsec
                  - mozilliansorg_secops-aws-admins
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AdministratorAccess
      MaxSessionDuration: 43200  # 12 hours
  ReadOnlyIAMRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: MAWS-ReadOnly
      Description: !Join [ '', [ 'ReadOnlyAccess Federated IAM Role which the group team_opsec is permitted to assume. This Role enables viewing sensitive data like S3 file contents, DynamoDB table contents, etc']]
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Principal:
              Federated: !Join [ '', [ 'arn:aws:iam::', !Ref 'AWS::AccountId', ':oidc-provider/auth.mozilla.auth0.com/' ]]
            Action: sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
            Effect: Allow
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                auth.mozilla.auth0.com/:aud: N7lULzWtfVUDGymwDs0yDEq6ZcwmFazj
              ForAnyValue:StringEquals:
                auth.mozilla.auth0.com/:amr:
                  - team_opsec
                  - mozilliansorg_secops-aws-admins
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/ReadOnlyAccess
      MaxSessionDuration: 43200  # 12 hours
  ViewOnlyIAMRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: MAWS-ViewOnly
      Description: !Join [ '', [ 'ViewOnlyAccess Federated IAM Role which the group team_opsec is permitted to assume. This Role enables viewing only resource metadata, not sensitive data like S3 file contents']]
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Principal:
              Federated: !Join [ '', [ 'arn:aws:iam::', !Ref 'AWS::AccountId', ':oidc-provider/auth.mozilla.auth0.com/' ]]
            Action: sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
            Effect: Allow
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                auth.mozilla.auth0.com/:aud: N7lULzWtfVUDGymwDs0yDEq6ZcwmFazj
              ForAnyValue:StringEquals:
                auth.mozilla.auth0.com/:amr:
                  - team_opsec
                  - mozilliansorg_secops-aws-admins
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/job-function/ViewOnlyAccess
      MaxSessionDuration: 43200  # 12 hours
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates three federated IAM roles for our AWS account to enable our security operations team to access AWS resources through our Auth0 identity provider, specifically using the OIDC provider endpoint auth.mozilla.auth0.com. The template must create an Admin role named MAWS-Admin with the AWS managed AdministratorAccess policy attached, a ReadOnly role named MAWS-ReadOnly with the AWS managed ReadOnlyAccess policy attached, and a ViewOnly role named MAWS-ViewOnly with the AWS managed job-function/ViewOnlyAccess policy attached. Each role must be assumable only via the sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity action from the federated principal arn:aws:iam::[account-id]:oidc-provider/auth.mozilla.auth0.com/, with a condition requiring the audience claim to equal N7lULzWtfVUDGymwDs0yDEq6ZcwmFazj and the amr claim to contain either team_opsec or mozilliansorg_secops-aws-admins. All three roles must have a maximum session duration of 12 hours (43200 seconds) to allow for extended operational sessions, and each role should have a descriptive description explaining its purpose and the permissions it grants, with the ReadOnly role noting it can view sensitive data like S3 file contents and DynamoDB table contents while the ViewOnly role explicitly states it only provides access to resource metadata and not sensitive data.

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a transit gateway and optionally provisions DMZ, inspection, and virtual firewall VPCs with VPN attachments for a compliant framework for federal and DoD workloads in AWS GovCloud US, built by wwps-proserve-us-dod. The template must accept parameters for the S3 bucket and region hosting the nested templates (e.g., using a bucket name like `my-bucket` and region `us-gov-west-1`), a repository path, the management services account ID, central account ID, and the AWS Organizations principal org ID. It should also accept boolean flags to enable or disable the directory VPC, external access VPC, VPC firewall (which creates both a DMZ VPC and an inspection VPC), and virtual firewall (which creates a firewall VPC with VPN attachments). The transit gateway’s Amazon side ASN must be retrieved from the SSM parameter `/compliant/framework/transit/transit-gateway/amazon-side-asn`. For each enabled feature, the template should store the corresponding enable flag in SSM parameters under paths like `/compliant/framework/transit/directory-vpc/enabled`, `/compliant/framework/transit/external-access-vpc/enabled`, `/compliant/framework/transit/vpc-firewall/enabled`, and `/compliant/framework/transit/virtual-firewall/enabled`. The nested stacks for the transit gateway, DMZ VPC, inspection VPC, virtual firewall VPC, and VPN attachment must be referenced from the S3 bucket using a template URL pattern like `https://${pS3Bucket}.${pS3Region}.amazonaws.com/${pRepo}/templates/transit-gateway.yml` (and similarly for `transit-dmz-vpc.yml`, `transit-inspection-vpc.yml`, `transit-firewall-vpc.yml`, and `transit-vpn-attachment.yml`). The DMZ and inspection VPC stacks must receive the transit gateway ID from the transit gateway stack output, the logging bucket ARN constructed as `arn:${AWS::Partition}:s3:::flow-logs-${pManagementServicesAccountId}-${AWS::Region}`, and the central account ID and principal org ID. The virtual firewall VPC stack must receive the transit gateway ID and logging bucket ARN, and its outputs for firewall A and B internal ENI public IP addresses must be passed to the VPN attachment stack along with the transit gateway ID. The template must conditionally create the DMZ VPC, inspection VPC, virtual firewall VPC, and VPN attachment stacks based on the enable flags, and store the resulting VPN connection IDs and firewall VPC transit gateway attachment ID in SSM parameters under `/compliant/framework/transit/firewall-vpc/tgw-attach/id`, `/compliant/framework/transit/firewall-vpc/vpn-connection/a/id`, and `/compliant/framework/transit/firewall-vpc/vpn-connection/b/id`,
